stories.title: Pope warns a 'paradise of machines' could undermine humanity as he opens France trip
stories.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV has warned that a "paradise of machines" could undermine humanity. He raises concerns about artificial intelligence, nuclear arms, and human rights during his visit to France.
stories.lead:
Pope Leo XIV warned Friday that a "paradise of machines" risked undermining humanity as he opened a trip to France by posing fundamental questions about what it means to be human in the age of artificial intelligence, a nuclear arms race and other threats to life itself.

Leo raised existential concerns about scientific progress, life and human rights during his opening speech to President Emmanuel Macron and authorities at the Élysée Palace and then to diplomats and United Nations employees at the headquarters of UNESCO, the U.N. culture and education organization.

stories.title: Bangkok roads submerged as flood disaster declared
stories.excerpt: An emergency has been declared across the capital of Thailand as days of heavy rain leave the city inundated.
stories.lead:
Disaster declared as heavy rain sparks Bangkok flooding

A flood emergency disaster has been declared across Bangkok after 48 hours of heavy rain left roads in the Thai capital submerged.

People have been urged to stay at home and those living close to the city's network of canals have been advised to move their belongings to upper floors.

stories.title: CNN left off Air Force One for Trump's upcoming trip, White House signals in new media restriction
stories.excerpt: The White House has signaled that CNN will be left off Air Force One for President Donald Trump's Saturday trip in the latest media restriction in an ongoing dispute with First Amendment implications.
stories.lead: CNN was replaced by the conservative Real America's Voice News. The news came just after journalists from three news outlets that Trump banned last week from the White House grounds returned to the executive complex with TV cameras, laptops and microphones in hand. Trump is scheduled travel to Knoxville, Tennessee, and attend a college football game between Tennessee and Texas.

stories.title: Bangkok declares disaster as heavy rains spark flooding
stories.excerpt: Days of near continuous downpours have caused widespread flooding in the Thai capital.
stories.lead:
Days of almost continuous heavy rains have caused widespread flooding in the Thai capital, with the city's governor declaring it a disaster-affected zone.

Almost 300 millimetres (11.8 inches) has fallen over the period, and more is expected in the coming days, according to Governor Chadchart Sittipunt.

Videos from Bangkok show cars trying to navigate roads that have been entirely submerged by the floodwaters, with some vehicles appearing stranded.

stories.title: The U.S. has more thalidomide survivors than the government admits
stories.excerpt: In the 1950s and 1960s, doctors gave the drug thalidomide to pregnant patients without telling them — and without FDA approval. Now those patients' children want recognition.
stories.lead:
When Cincinnati-based pharmaceutical company William S. Merrell applied for Food and Drug Administration approval for a German-made sedative in late 1960, it expected the application to sail through the process and be on store shelves in time for Christmas.

The drug, thalidomide, was not approved that year or the next. A persistent medical reviewer at the FDA kept the drug from being approved for general use. Dr. Frances Oldham Kelsey's actions fundamentally changed the agency's testing and approval process, leading to the robust regulations that exist today.

stories.title: Scottish drivers hit as diesel passes £2 a litre across the country
stories.excerpt: Motoring organisation the RAC says it expects the average UK diesel price to hit a new record high over the weekend.
stories.lead:
Analysis by BBC Scotland News suggests there are at least 226 sites - stretching from the Borders to Shetland - where the price of a litre of diesel is greater than £2.

Some of the highest prices are in island and rural areas, including 238.8p and 223p in the Hebrides and 209.0p and 208.9p in the Northern Isles.

South Uist-based haulier Norman MacAskill said it cost 32p a litre to fill a lorry's tank when he started in the haulage business 40 years ago, but it was now £2.22.

stories.excerpt: Maureen Bougeard says some prospective volunteers do not respond after learning about expenses.
stories.lead:
A delivery service offering meals to people in need has spoken about the challenges of recruiting new volunteers due to rising fuel costs.

Maureen Bougeard said Meals on Wheels Jersey had received £38,000 from the Jersey Community Foundation to fund work supplying hot meals to islanders who are unable to prepare meals themselves.

She said the service packed and delivered meals to about 100 people, four days a week - but added fuel costs were having an impact.

stories.title: Gannon University Overpowers Mercyhurst University, 23-16, to Start Laker Invitational
stories.excerpt: Host Mercyhurst University fell to Gannon University, 23-16, in the first game of the Laker Invitational at the Hallman Aquatic Center. The post Gannon University Overpowers Mercyhurst University, 23-16, to Start Laker Invitational appeared first on Collegiate Water Polo Association .
stories.lead:
ERIE, Pa. – Host Mercyhurst University fell to Gannon University, 23-16, in the first game of the Laker Invitational at the Hallman Aquatic Center.

The Lakers brought the heat to the pool in the first quarter with Petar Vujovic providing the game’s first goal. The Golden Knights retaliated by scoring a goal of their own to make the game one-all with seven minutes to go. Gannon continued to build off that momentum by scoring three more to break the tie. Aiden Botterilll got on the board for Mercyhurst, narrowing the Golden Knights’ lead to two at the end of one quarter.

stories.title: Water Polo Comes Up Short at #1 UCLA
stories.excerpt: Water polo falls at #1 UCLA, 16-11.
stories.lead:
Los Angeles, Calif. – Though he plays a different sport, Cristiano Ronaldo once said, "To Be The Best You Need The Best." The Fordham water polo squad is taking that to heart this weekend, playing three nationally-ranked opponents this weekend in southern California, beginning with tonight's match against #1 UCLA. The Rams gave a valiant effort against the defending national champions before falling to the Bruins, 16-11, at the Spieker Aquatics Center.

With the loss, Fordham falls to 9-1 on the season while UCLA improves to 13-0.

The Bruins led 4-0 after the first quarter and extended the lead to 5-0 early in the second.
